answer: A farm reuses one playbook across many names, so force each name to migrate. Each epoch, assign every identity a fresh, random venue — a different tool, format, and task — with a short deadline to produce venue-specific work a template cannot fake. A lone sparrow learns its new juniper branch quickly; clones arrive together in a spiral of identical timing, errors, and phrasing, or migrate one by one at linear cost. Synchronized arrivals mark the cluster, and shared templates die in the new venue.
